Research

My research lies at the intersection of statistics, machine learning, and healthcare. I study how predictive models, real-world evidence, and clinical knowledge can support reliable decisions.

Research interests

From predicting risk to understanding when, why, and how to act.

  • Statistical learning and clinical decision-making. Developing interpretable prediction methods that transfer across settings and connect risk estimates with clinical actions and resource constraints.
  • Causal inference and real-world evidence. Studying treatment strategies, patient heterogeneity, and evolving health trajectories through target trial emulation and longitudinal modeling.
  • Knowledge-centric and trustworthy clinical AI. Integrating clinical guidelines, knowledge graphs, and adaptive reasoning to support decisions under incomplete and changing information.

Publications & manuscripts

* Equal contribution

2026Submitted · JAMIA

ActionRef: Learning Reference Thresholds and Guiding Clinical Risk Threshold Selection

Huang, X., Patel, S., Jin, Y., Mai, X., Chu, C., Hou, J., Puskarich, M. A., and Xie, F.

Learning behavioral reference thresholds and making clinical operating trade-offs explicit.

Code ↗Documentation ↗
My contribution

I developed a general framework that learns reference risk thresholds from observed clinical actions and guides selection under workload constraints. I led multicenter evaluation and packaged the method as reusable Python software.

2026Workshop · Accepted

RADAR: A Guideline-Grounded Multi-Agent System for the Emergency-Department Sepsis Pathway

Jin, Y.*, Huang, X.*, Chandu, H. P., Xiong, X., Lin, M., and Xie, F.

NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on GenAI4Health · Demonstration Paper Track

Paper ↗Code & demo ↗
My contribution

As a co-first author, I co-developed a guideline-grounded system that connects clinical knowledge graphs with a shared patient state. I built core patient-data and evidence-integration workflows and contributed to the public software package and interactive demo.

2026Accepted · eClinicalMedicine

Development and Multicenter External Validation of a Data-Driven Scoring System for Early and Rapid Identification of Sepsis in Emergency Departments

Jin, Y., Huang, X., Wang, Y., Wacker, D. A., Puskarich, M. A., and Xie, F.

Preprint available on medRxiv

Preprint ↗Code ↗
My contribution

I co-developed an interpretable sepsis risk score using more than 2.2 million emergency-department encounters. My work included cohort harmonization and model-development and external-validation workflows across UMN, MIMIC-IV-ED, and Stanford MC-MED.
